memory_candidates.content: In jq, `EXPR | index(ARG)` evaluates ARG against EXPR's output (the piped value), not the original '.' before the pipe. Writing `select(($array_var | index(.field)) != null)` inside a larger pipeline is a common bug: '.field' silently tries to index $array_var itself, raising 'Cannot index array with string'. Fix: bind the scalar first with `as`, e.g. `select(.field as $v | ($array_var | index($v)) != null)`, which evaluates 'as' against the current '.' (preserving it) before piping only the bound value onward.

When a plan's Non-Goal explicitly bars a new component from becoming an admission/blocking gate, be careful not to overclaim in documentation that a related guardrail's 'exclude by default' clause is now fully satisfied just because the 'warn loudly' half was implemented -- verify by tracing whether the actual dispatch-eligibility code path (e.g. dependency_graph construction) would truly exclude the case, not just whether a new report surfaces it.
